accounts.prose: `catalog` exposes `lookup`, coordinating keyed retrieval rather than implementing storage or remote access itself. It rejects an empty key; on a cache hit it returns the stored value; on a miss it awaits `readRemote`, stores the returned value with `remember`, then returns it. Because storage occurs only after the awaited read completes, a rejected remote request is not cached. The nearby README describes the same sequence.

accounts.prose: `cache` owns mutable in-process storage. `cached(key)` returns the value only when its sole entry has the same key; `remember(key, value)` replaces that entry. It is therefore a one-entry last-write cache, not a catalog replica.

accounts.prose: `remote` owns adapter selection and invocation. It starts with the name `./adapter`; `configureAdapter(name)` replaces that name, and `readRemote(key)` dynamically loads the currently named adapter and calls its `read(key)` operation. Thus transport, returned data, failures, and even the concrete adapter remain delegated beyond the analyzed modules.

CommonJS loading requests are recognized only when a direct call names the standard loader with one argument, local naming is fully checked, and the captured module environment supports that loader. Renamed loaders, object methods and other loading APIs are excluded.

A file explicitly identified as using the ECMAScript module system is not treated as using the CommonJS loader, even if declarations describe that loader. When configuration preserves the written module system, a declaration must additionally establish that the loader can be called. Missing module configuration does not establish a default.
Computed requested names are not evaluated. A located file outside the discovered module population does not add a module or establish a dependency edge.

qualification.guarantee: Repository-layout relationships are established from the captured visible worktree artifact population.
limitations: Current worktree inputs are first-observed, not an atomic filesystem transaction.
Git reads live exclusion policy; a final policy check detects lasting changes, not transient concurrent edits.
Sparse-checkout completeness is unresolved; absent worktree contents are not reconstructed.
Effective local and user-global exclusions can change visibility across environments.
Nested repositories and submodules are opaque, unanalyzed boundary artifacts.
Links resolve only through captured paths, with at most 40 redirects; traversal outside the provider is refused.
An existing link target without an exact captured path spelling is not established as a region or artifact.
Repository layout is one organizational account, not a claim about architectural purpose.
README association establishes only direct documentation existence, not truth, currency, completeness, or inheritance.
